 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Rajiv Roy
 Oral Order
2 17-02-2023
Heard Mr. Kaushal Kumar Jha, learned Senior Counsel for the petitioners and learned APP for the State.

The petitioner has come before this Court for quashing of the FIR vide Jakkanpur P.S. Case No. 278 of 2020 registered under sections 498A & 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.

As per the prosecution story, the marriage of the opposite party no.2 was solemnized on 25.02.2020 with the petitioner no.1 Dr. Anand Kumar and within couple of days, situation came to such a stage that on 1.3.2020, the couple took Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.44446 of 2022(2) dt.17-02-2023 separate ways.

sentences.text: 1 Learned Senior Counsel further submits that later both of them came to a negotiating table which culminated with the dissolution of their marriage vide Matrimonial Case No. 716 of 2021 on 23.4.2022.
Learned Senior Counsel has taken this Court to the detailed order passed by the learned Principal Judge, Family Court, Patna which took note of the agreement made between the parties.

Learned Senior Counsel also referred to the order of Supreme Court of India in Rangappa Javoor vs.
The State of Karnataka and Another reported in 2023 Live Law (SC)74 in which Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
It is apparent that the parties have resolved and settled their disputes.

sentences.text: In the facts of the cases, we do not feel that any useful purpose would be served by continuation of the prosecution.
The appellant-Rangappa Javoor, who is an officer in the Boarder Security Force and as per the job requirement, has to serve in different parts of the country, would be put to harassment.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.44446 of 2022(2) dt.17-02-2023

This court has held that in cases of offences relating to matrimonial disputes, if the Court is satisfied that the parties have genuinely settled the disputes amicably, then for the purpose of securing ends of justice, criminal proceedings inter-se parties can be quashed by exercising the powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India or even under Section 482 of Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
Issue notice to opposite party no.2

both by registered cover with A/D as well as ordinary process for which requisites etc. must be filed within two weeks from today failing which this application shall stand dismissed without further reference to a Bench.

In the meantime, no coercive steps will be taken against the petitioner in connection with Jakkanpur P.S. Case No. 278 of 2020 pending in the Court of A.C.J.M.-1st,
Patna.

(Rajiv Roy, J) Ravi/-
